headline: High risk of shared-workspace leakage and cascading errors; Cursor’s default editor/clipboard/MCP surfaces can ingest CrewAI outputs without provenance checks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can write to the host working directory and emit stdout, while Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents by default. That creates a plausible injection bridge if CrewAI output is copied or saved into files Cursor treats as trusted. No shared MCP is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF CrewAI output is written into a file or pasted into Cursor buffers, Cursor may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF the operator enables copy-paste or file handoff between the two agents, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep CrewAI and Cursor on separate workspaces.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Require a human review step before Cursor consumes CrewAI output.
Use a read-only export format for CrewAI outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to files passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents. Because Cursor’s shared state is via local filesystem and CrewAI writes the host working directory, sensitive data can flow into Cursor’s context in default workflows. The pair is not documented as isolated, so leakage is plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF CrewAI processes secrets or sensitive crew inputs and writes them to files, Cursor can ingest them from the workspace.
IF the operator copies CrewAI output into Cursor, clipboard contents may expose sensitive data.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in CrewAI task inputs.
Store CrewAI outputs in a separate directory excluded from Cursor.
Turn off clipboard sharing between tools.
Redact sensitive fields before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write, shell execution, and subprocess spawning. Cursor also modifies git state and shares state via the local filesystem, while CrewAI writes the host working directory with no default self-isolation. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite files or corrupt git state without locking, matching the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or working directory, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Cursor auto-runs commands while CrewAI also writes files, race conditions can corrupt state.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate clone.
Disable Cursor Yolo mode during shared work.
Serialize file writes with a human gate.
Use git branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit outputs from role-playing agents, and Cursor’s agent loop can act on workspace content and tool outputs. If Cursor treats CrewAI-produced text as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into code changes or commands. This is a default-pathway risk, not just an edge case.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes CrewAI-generated plans, code, or facts without verification, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF CrewAI outputs are pasted into Cursor as instructions, Cursor may execute them as authoritative.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before Cursor acts on CrewAI output.
Use checklists for any generated code or commands.
Separate planning from execution roles.
Ask a human to confirm high-impact steps.
requires-engineering: add structured schemas and validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and may send data to model providers and api.cursor.sh. If regulated or sensitive data is present, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across two vendors. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into CrewAI tasks and then opened in Cursor, both vendors may process it.
IF the operator relies on different retention or privacy policies, compliance obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Review vendor privacy and retention settings before use.
Use synthetic or masked data for development.
Document data-flow boundaries for the pair.
requires-engineering: obtain legal/compliance approval and DPA review.
